mainTopic: How the ערי מקלט were set up and made livable, the value of תורה learning, and אגדות about the cities of refuge
overview: The גמרא explains how the ערי מקלט were spaced. They were placed closer to places with many murderers, like גלעד and שכם, and the six main cities protect even a killer who came there without meaning to take refuge, unlike the 42 cities of the לוים. It answers questions about חברון and קדש, and then quotes a ברייתא: an עיר מקלט must be a medium-sized town with water, markets and people, where the גואל הדם has no reason to come. רבי יצחק learns all this from the word 'וָחָי', 'and live', which also teaches that a student's רב, or a רב's ישיבה, goes into גלות with him. The גמרא asks how this fits with רבי יוחנן's teaching that Torah itself protects. It answers that Torah protects only while one is learning, or that it protects from the מלאך המות, as the story of רב חסדא shows. Next come אגדות about the ערי מקלט: why ראובן's city comes first, how משה 'made the sun shine' for killers, and how משה grabbed a מצוה even when it would not take effect yet. A פסוק in קהלת is then read in several ways about teaching the public and learning with others. Teachings by רבי יהושע בן לוי praise the power of תורה learning. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's line about roads to the ערי מקלט, opening a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that murderers were common in גלעד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק calling גלעד 'covered with blood,' and רבי אלעזר explains that its people would lie in ambush to kill.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'גלעד is a city of those who do evil, covered with blood.' What does 'covered with blood' mean? רבי אלעזר says: they would lie in ambush to kill people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove the point made just before this: there were many murderers in גלעד. That is why גלעד needed more ערי מקלט than its size would suggest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עֲקֻבָּה in the פסוק could just mean 'stained' or 'marked.' רבי אלעזר reads it as coming from the root עקב, 'to lie in wait.' So the פסוק describes people who planned murders on purpose, which shows that killing was common there.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying in ambush, waiting to attack

phrases.english: As it is written: "Gilead is a city of those who work iniquity,
phrases.notes: הושע 6:8

phrases.english: covered with blood"
What is "covered with blood"?
Rabbi Elazar says:
That they would lie in ambush to kill people.
phrases.notes: It's a play on sound: the פסוק's word עֲקֻבָּה and עוֹקְבִין come from the same root.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: גִּלְעָד קִרְיַת פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן

steps.title: Why is the middle city of refuge placed so close?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ערי מקלט near the southern and northern borders are far from the edge, while the middle city is close to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the cities on this side and on that side, that they are far away, and what is different about the middle one, that it is close?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the layout of the ערי מקלט. If the cities are meant to serve everyone equally, why is the middle one easier to reach than the outer ones?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outer cities sit about a quarter of the land's length from each border, so someone at the edge has a long trip. The middle city, שכם, is reached by a much shorter trip from either side. The גמרא wants to know why the middle area gets this extra closeness.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asking why two cases are treated differently)

phrases.english: And what is different about this side
phrases.notes: This refers to the spacing described just before: the outer cities are a quarter of the land away from each border.

phrases.english: and that side, that they are far,
and what is different about the middle ones, that they are close?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מֵהַאי גִּיסָא וּמֵהַאי גִּיסָא דִּמְרַחֲקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from גלעד to a new question about the uneven spacing of the cities on the western side of the ירדן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The layout of the ערי מקלט, where the middle city is closer than the outer ones
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cities are spaced to serve everyone fairly, the middle region should not get easier access than the border regions.

steps.title: אביי: murderers were common in שכם too
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that murderers were common in שכם, so a city of refuge needed to be close by. He proves it from a פסוק, which רבי אלעזר explains.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: murderers were also common in שכם, as it is written: 'As troops of robbers wait for a man, so does the band of priests; they murder on the way to שכם.' What is 'band of priests'? רבי אלעזר says: they would band together to kill people, just like כהנים band together to divide תרומה at the threshing floors.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The middle city is closer because שכם, like גלעד, had many killers, so more people there needed quick access to a city of refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same reasoning used for גלעד now explains שכם: the spacing follows where killings actually happen, not just distance. רבי אלעזר reads 'band of priests' as a comparison. Just as כהנים gather in groups at the threshing floors to get תרומה, these killers gathered in groups to murder.

keyTerms.meaning: A band or group of priests
The threshing floors, where grain is collected

steps.whatToRemember: The ערי מקלט were not spaced evenly by distance alone. They were placed closer to places where killings were common, like גלעד and שכם.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In Shechem, too, murderers are common,

That they would band together to kill people,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁכֶם נָמֵי שְׁכִיחִי רוֹצְחִים

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cities should be spaced evenly, so the middle city's closeness seems unfair.
steps.terutzMaskana: Murderers were common in שכם, so the city of refuge there needed to be easy to reach.

steps.title: Aren't there 42 more cities of refuge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that there are only six ערי מקלט, since the תורה says to give 42 more cities to the לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there no more? But it is written: 'And besides them you shall give forty-two cities.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count of six ערי מקלט. A פסוק seems to say that the 42 cities of the לוים also count as places of refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first mentions the six ערי מקלט and then says 'besides them' to give 42 more cities. Mentioning them together suggests the 42 also protect a killer. If so, why does the discussion speak only of six?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opening a challenge from a פסוק)
Forty-two cities (the other cities of the לוים)

phrases.english: And are there no more?
But isn't it written:
"And besides them you shall give forty-two cities"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:6. 'Them' means the six ערי מקלט, and the 42 are the other cities given to the לוים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ לֵיכָּא? וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the cities are placed to how many cities of refuge there really are.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that there are only six ערי מקלט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists the 42 cities of the לוים together with the six, which suggests they also protect a killer.

steps.title: אביי: the six protect always, the 42 only with intent
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the six main cities protect a killer even if he came there without meaning to take refuge. The 42 cities of the לוים protect him only if he came there on purpose to take refuge.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: these six protect whether the killer came knowingly or not knowingly. Those 42 protect only if he came knowingly; if not knowingly, they do not protect.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. The 42 cities really are places of refuge, but they work under a narrower rule than the six main cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 42 cities are not denied the status of refuge; they simply have a weaker form of protection. The six main cities protect a killer automatically, even if he just happened to be there. The 42 protect only someone who came there with the intention of taking refuge. That is why the six are counted as the main ערי מקלט.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowingly, with intent to take refuge
Unknowingly, without intent to take refuge

steps.whatToRemember: All 48 cities give refuge. The six main ones protect even someone who arrived without that intention, while the 42 cities of the לוים protect only someone who came on purpose to take refuge.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the 42 cities are not cities of refuge at all. They do protect, but only a killer who came there on purpose to take refuge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a פסוק that seems to make 48 cities of refuge fits with the focus on six. All of them protect, but under different conditions.

phrases.english: Abaye said: These,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the six main ערי מקלט; the second 'those' below means the 42 cities of the לוים.

phrases.english: take in and protect, whether he came knowingly
phrases.notes: 'Knowingly' means he came there intending to take refuge.

phrases.english: or not knowingly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַלָּלוּ, קוֹלְטוֹת בֵּין לְדַעַת בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 about the 42 cities.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction between the two kinds of cities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 42 cities seem to be exactly like the six, so there should be 48 equal cities of refuge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The six protect a killer whether or not he came intending refuge; the 42 protect only one who came intending refuge.

steps.title: How could חברון be an עיר מקלט if it was given to כלב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how חברון could be an עיר מקלט when a פסוק says it was given to כלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was חברון really a city of refuge? But the פסוק says, 'They gave חברון to כלב, as משה had said!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that חברון was one of the ערי מקלט. A פסוק says חברון was handed over to כלב as his own city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערי מקלט were cities of the לוים. If חברון belonged to כלב, who was from שבט יהודה, it seems it could not be a city of the לוים, and so it could not be a city of refuge.

keyTerms.meaning: A city of refuge, where an accidental killer can run to for safety
But isn't it written? (a challenge from a פסוק)
כלב בן יפנה, from שבט יהודה, who was promised חברון

phrases.english: And was Hebron a city of refuge?
But isn't it written:
"And they gave Hebron to Caleb
phrases.notes: שופטים 1:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about whether a specific city on the list of ערי מקלט could really have served that role.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חברון was an עיר מקלט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says חברון was given to כלב of שבט יהודה, so it seems it was not a city of the לוים, and only cities of the לוים could be ערי מקלט.

steps.title: כלב received only the outskirts of חברון
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that כלב got only the fields and villages around חברון, not the city itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: כלב got its outskirts, as the פסוק says, 'The field of the city and its villages they gave to כלב בן יפנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. Only the land around חברון went to כלב, while the city itself stayed a city of the לוים and an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי shows from another פסוק that the gift to כלב was the fields and villages around the city. So the פסוק in שופטים means the area of חברון, and the city itself could still be an עיר מקלט.

keyTerms.meaning: Its outskirts, the area surrounding the city

phrases.english: Abaye said: Its outskirts,
phrases.notes: He means כלב got only the area around חברון, not the city itself.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"And the field of the city and its villages
they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh."
phrases.notes: יהושע 21:12

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: פַּרְווֹדֶהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the פסוק by quoting a second פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole city of חברון was given to כלב, so it could not be a city of the לוים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the fields and villages around חברון went to כלב; the city itself was an עיר מקלט.

steps.title: קדש is listed as a fortified city, but ערי מקלט must be medium-sized
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how קדש could be an עיר מקלט when a פסוק lists it among the big fortified cities, and a ברייתא says ערי מקלט must be medium-sized towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was קדש really a city of refuge? But the פסוק lists it among the fortified cities, and a ברייתא teaches that ערי מקלט may not be small settlements or large cities, only medium-sized towns!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge, now about קדש. It puts together a פסוק and a ברייתא to show that קדש seems to be the wrong size to be a city of refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls קדש a fortified city, which sounds like a big, walled city. The ברייתא says ערי מקלט must be medium-sized towns, not big cities. So קדש seems to be too big to be an עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: And was Kedesh a city of refuge?
But isn't it written:
"And the fortified cities were Tziddim, Tzer,
and Chammat, Rakkat, and Kinneret, etc.,
and Kedesh, and Edrei, and Ein Chatzor",
and it was taught: These cities

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן לֹא טִירִין קְטַנִּים
phrases.english: one does not make them small settlements
nor large cities,
but only medium-sized towns!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same kind as step 6, now about a different city.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קדש was an עיר מקלט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק calls קדש a fortified (big) city, but a ברייתא says ערי מקלט must be medium-sized towns.

steps.title: There were two places called קדש
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that there were two different cities named קדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: There were two cities called קדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question about קדש. The fortified קדש in the פסוק is a different city from the קדש that was an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction, because the two sources are not talking about the same place. The big fortified קדש was one city, and the medium-sized קדש was the city of refuge.

keyTerms.meaning: קדש, a city in the north listed as one of the ערי מקלט

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: תַּרְתֵּי קֶדֶשׁ הֲוַאי.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: There were two cities called Kedesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: תַּרְתֵּי קֶדֶשׁ הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: two different places with the same name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fortified קדש and the city of refuge קדש are the same city.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were two separate cities with the same name.

steps.title: קדש was like סליקום and the fortress of סליקום
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: קדש was a town with a separate fortress next to it, like סליקום and its fortress.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is like סליקום and the fortress of סליקום.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another answer to the question about קדש. He compares it to a known place, סליקום, which had a town and a fortress beside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי agrees there were two places, but they were connected: a medium-sized town and a fortress next to it, both called by the same name. The fortress is the 'fortified city' in the פסוק, and the town itself was the עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
phrases.notes: Some versions put the word אמר before רב אשי and some after; the meaning is the same.

phrases.english: It is like Selikum and the fortress of Selikum.
phrases.notes: סליקום was a town with its own separate fortress next to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן סְלֵיקוּם וְאַקְרָא דִּסְלֵיקוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of step 8, alongside רב יוסף's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a known example of a town with an attached fortress
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fortified קדש is the same place as the city of refuge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fortress of קדש was the fortified city, and the town of קדש next to it was the medium-sized עיר מקלט.

steps.title: How the cities of refuge must be set up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the full ברייתא: ערי מקלט must be medium-sized, with water, markets and a large population, and they must be kept that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא itself: These cities are not made small settlements or large cities, only medium-sized towns. They are placed only where there is water, and if there is no water, water is brought to them. They are placed only where there are markets and where there are many people. If the population around them shrinks, more people are added. If the residents of the city shrink, כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are brought there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the whole ברייתא that it used in step 8. It lists the conditions that a city must have to be an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beyond the size rule, the city must have water, markets and plenty of people coming through. These things are not a one-time check: if the population goes down, the community must add more people. The killer has to stay there, so the city has to be a place where a person can really live.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; the גמרא goes back to discuss a source it quoted earlier
They place or set up (the cities)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different population rules here. The first (אוכלוסיהן) is about the number of people in the area around the city; the second (דיוריהן) is about the people who actually live inside the city.

phrases.english: The matter itself: These cities,
phrases.notes: The גמרא goes back to quote the full ברייתא from step 8.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן לֹא טִירִין קְטַנִּים
phrases.english: one does not make them small settlements

but only medium-sized towns.

and if there is no water there,

phrases.english: And one places them only in a place of markets,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערי מקלט must be medium-sized towns with water, markets and many people, and the community must keep them populated.

steps.title: Argument about selling weapons and hunting tools in cities of refuge
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says weapons and trapping tools may not be sold in ערי מקלט; חכמים allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Weapons and trapping tools may not be sold there; this is רבי נחמיה's view. The חכמים allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a מחלוקת. רבי נחמיה forbids selling weapons and trapping tools in the ערי מקלט, and the חכמים permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה adds a safety rule to protect the killer who lives there. The חכמים do not make this rule about selling weapons and trapping tools.

phrases.english: And one does not sell in them

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כְּלֵי זַיִין, וְלֹא כְּלֵי מְצוּדָה,
phrases.english: neither weapons nor trapping tools;
these are the words of Rabbi Nechemya.
And the Sages permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מוֹכְרִין בָּהֶן לֹא כְּלֵי זַיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new rule, this time a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נחמיה forbids selling weapons and trapping tools in ערי מקלט; the חכמים permit it.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no nets or ropes in cities of refuge
steps.stepSummary: Both רבי נחמיה and חכמים agree that nets may not be spread and ropes may not be twisted in ערי מקלט, so the גואל הדם will not come there often.
steps.simpleTranslation: They agree that nets are not spread in them and ropes are not twisted in them, so that the foot of the גואל הדם will not be common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a rule that both sides accept. Making nets and ropes is not allowed in the ערי מקלט, and the ברייתא gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These trades would bring customers into the city, and one of them could be the גואל הדם. The goal is to keep the גואל הדם from having a reason to visit the place where the killer lives. Even the חכמים, who allowed selling weapons, agree to this.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood avenger, the relative of the person who was killed

steps.whatToRemember: An עיר מקלט had to be a real, livable town (medium size, water, markets, people), and it had to stay a safe place where the גואל הדם would have no reason to show up.

phrases.english: And they agree that one does not spread nets in them,
and one does not twist ropes in them,
so that the foot
of the blood avenger will not be common there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאֵין פּוֹרְסִין בְּתוֹכָן מְצוּדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the מחלוקת of step 12 with a point both sides agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that nets may not be spread and ropes may not be twisted in ערי מקלט, so the גואל הדם will not come there often.

steps.title: The verse behind making the city livable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the source for all the rules about keeping ערי מקלט comfortable is the word 'וָחָי', 'and live'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What פסוק teaches this? 'And he shall flee to one of these cities and live.' This means: do whatever is needed so that he can really live there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives the Torah source for the rules in Steps 11-13: water, markets, people, and keeping the גואל הדם away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וָחָי' is not only a promise that the killer will be safe. It is read as a command: give him a real life in the city. That is why the city needs water, markets and a population.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And live'; the key word in the פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This one word, 'וָחָי', becomes the source for the next two rulings as well.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says: What is the verse?

phrases.aramaic: ״וְנָס אֶל אַחַת מִן הֶעָרִים הָאֵל וָחָי״
phrases.english: 'And he shall flee to one of these cities and live'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:42

phrases.english: Do something for him
so that he will have life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יצחק מאי קרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the rules in Steps 11-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'וָחָי' requires that the exile be given everything he needs to truly live in the עיר מקלט.

steps.title: A student's teacher goes into exile with him
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that when a תלמיד goes into גלות, his רב goes with him, based on 'וָחָי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: When a student is exiled, his teacher is sent with him, as it says 'and live', meaning: do what is needed so that he can really live.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא applies the same word 'וָחָי' to a new case: a תלמיד in גלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Torah learner, real life includes learning Torah. So 'giving him life' means bringing his רב to the עיר מקלט, so his learning does not stop.

keyTerms.meaning: Went into גלות (exile) to an עיר מקלט

steps.confusionAlert: The רב did not do anything wrong. He goes along only so the תלמיד can keep learning, not as a punishment.

phrases.english: It was taught: A student who was exiled
they exile his teacher with him,
as it is stated: 'and live'
Do something for him
so that he will have life.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנא תלמיד שגלה מגלין רבו עמו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from Step 14 for a new halacha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a תלמיד is sent to an עיר מקלט, his רב is sent with him so the תלמיד can keep learning.

steps.title: Do not teach an unworthy student
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירא learns from this that a person should not teach a student who is not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירא said: From here we learn that a person should not teach a student who is not worthy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זעירא draws a practical lesson from the rule in Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רב must follow his תלמיד into גלות, then teaching a careless or unworthy student can end with the teacher being exiled because of him. So be careful whom you teach.

keyTerms.meaning: From here; we learn from this

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira says: From here
that a person should not teach
a student who is not fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי זעירא מכאן שלא ישנה אדם לתלמיד שאינו הגון
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from the rule in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should not teach an unworthy student.

steps.title: A רב's ישיבה goes into גלות with him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that when a רב goes into גלות, his ישיבה goes with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: When a teacher is exiled, his ישיבה is exiled with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the reverse case: now the רב is the one in גלות, so his students come with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a רב, 'life' means teaching and learning with his students. So to give him 'וָחָי', his ישיבה moves with him to the עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: A teacher who was exiled
they exile his yeshiva with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן הרב שגלה מגלין ישיבתו עמו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of Step 15: the רב is exiled, and his students follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a רב is sent to an עיר מקלט, his ישיבה goes with him.

steps.title: But Torah itself protects like a city of refuge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: How can a רב be exiled at all? רבי יוחנן himself said that Torah protects a person like an עיר מקלט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי יוחנן said: How do we know that words of Torah give protection? The פסוק says 'בצר in the wilderness', and right after that it says 'And this is the Torah'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 17 using a different statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of ערי מקלט is placed right next to 'וזאת התורה', which teaches that Torah protects like an עיר מקלט. If so, a רב full of Torah should be protected wherever he is, so why would he need to go into גלות at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Give refuge, protect like an עיר מקלט
One of the ערי מקלט משה set aside

steps.confusionAlert: Both statements are from the same רבי יוחנן, so the גמרא is asking how his two rulings fit together.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
From where do we know that words of Torah give refuge?
As it is stated: 'Bezer in the wilderness, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:43

phrases.english: [and it is written after it:] 'And this is the Torah.'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:44. The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: איני והא אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a רב who is exiled brings his ישיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If Torah protects like an עיר מקלט, a רב should not need גלות, so there is no reason to move his ישיבה.

steps.title: Torah protects only while one is learning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: Torah protects while a person is learning; when he is not learning, he needs the עיר מקלט.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a contradiction. This one is when he is busy learning Torah, and that one is when he is not busy learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by splitting the two statements into two different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the רב is actually learning, the Torah protects him like an עיר מקלט. But nobody learns every moment, so in the other times he needs the real עיר מקלט, and he goes there with his ישיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: 'וָחָי' means the exile must truly live: a תלמיד's רב goes with him, and a רב's ישיבה goes with him. Torah protects like an עיר מקלט only while one is actually learning.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is at the time that he is engaged in it,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that Torah protects; 'it' means Torah learning.

phrases.english: that is at the time that he is not engaged in it.
phrases.notes: 'That' is the rule that the רב goes into exile with his yeshiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא קשיא הא בעידנא דעסיק בה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Torah protects a scholar at all times, so a רב would never need גלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah protects only while he is actually learning; at other times he needs the עיר מקלט, so he goes there with his ישיבה.

steps.title: A second answer: Torah protects from the מלאך המות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to understand רבי יוחנן's statement that Torah gives refuge: it protects a person from the מלאך המות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer: what does 'Torah gives refuge' mean? It protects from the Angel of Death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question from Step 18. Torah's 'refuge' is not about the גואל הדם at all; it is protection from the מלאך המות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the answer was that Torah protects only while one is learning. Here the גמרא changes the meaning of 'קולטין' itself. If Torah protects from death and not from the גואל הדם, there is no contradiction: a רב who killed by accident still needs an עיר מקלט.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say' — introduces a second, alternative answer
Give refuge, protect (like an עיר מקלט)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What does 'they give refuge' mean? From the Angel of Death.
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי יוחנן's line that words of Torah give refuge (Step 18).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, מַאי קוֹלְטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the קשיא of Step 18, as an alternative to Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Torah gives refuge from the גואל הדם, so a רב should never need גלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah gives refuge from the מלאך המות, so a רב who killed by accident still goes to an עיר מקלט.

steps.title: The story of רב חסדא and the cedar tree
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המות's messenger could not reach רב חסדא while he was learning. When a cedar cracked and רב חסדא stopped for a moment, the messenger took him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רב חסדא: he sat learning in the study hall, and the Angel of Death's messenger could not come near him, because he never stopped learning. The messenger climbed onto the cedar of the study hall. The cedar cracked, רב חסדא fell silent, and the messenger overpowered him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show that Torah learning really protects from the מלאך המות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves the idea of Step 20: as long as רב חסדא kept learning, death could not reach him. It also shows the protection works only during active learning. One moment of silence was enough for the messenger to take him.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall, the בית מדרש

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties both answers together: Torah's protection, whether from the גואל הדם or from death, depends on actually learning right now.

phrases.english: Like this incident of רב חסדא:
he was sitting and learning in the study hall of רב,
and was not able
the messenger [of the Angel of Death]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: to come near him,
because his mouth never stopped learning.
He went up and sat on the cedar of the study hall of רב.
The cedar cracked, and he fell silent,
phrases.notes: The one who fell silent is רב חסדא, startled by the noise.

phrases.english: and he overpowered him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא הֲוָה יָתֵיב וְגָרֵיס בְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports the answer of Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That Torah learning protects from the מלאך המות, only while one is learning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב חסדא's death in the study hall.

steps.title: Why ראובן's city is listed first
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי says ראובן's city is listed first among the ערי מקלט because ראובן was the first to try to save יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי said: Why did ראובן merit to be counted first in the rescue? Because he was the first to start a rescue, as it says: 'And ראובן heard and saved him from their hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the halacha to an אגדה about the ערי מקלט. It explains why the first city of refuge in the list is in ראובן's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עיר מקלט is a place of rescue. ראובן was the first to rescue, when he saved יוסף from his brothers, so he was rewarded by being first in the list of rescue cities. It is measure for measure.

phrases.english: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי said:
Why did ראובן merit
to be counted first in the rescue?
phrases.notes: The first עיר מקלט listed, בצר, is in ראובן's land (דברים 4:43).

phrases.english: Because he was the first to start a rescue,
as it says:
'And ראובן heard and saved him from their hands.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 37:21

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בַּר חֲנִילַאי: מִפְּנֵי מָה זָכָה רְאוּבֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of אגדות about the ערי מקלט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראובן's city is first among the ערי מקלט because ראובן was first to rescue יוסף.

steps.title: משה made the sun shine for killers
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי reads 'מזרחה שמש' as a hint: הקדוש ברוך הוא told משה to make the sun shine for killers, or praised him for having done so.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי taught: What does it mean, 'Then משה set apart three cities across the ירדן, toward the sunrise'? הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה: Make the sun shine for killers. Some say He said: You have made the sun shine for killers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי explains a פסוק about the ערי מקלט by playing on the word 'sunrise.' The cities give light and hope to an accidental killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מזרחה שמש' literally just mean 'east.' רבי שמלאי reads them as 'make the sun rise,' meaning give the killer a way out of darkness. The two versions differ only in whether it was a command ('make it shine') or praise after the fact ('you made it shine').

phrases.english: רבי שמלאי taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'Then משה set apart three cities
across the ירדן, toward the sunrise'?
phrases.notes: דברים 4:41. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; the whole דרשה rests on it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה:
Make the sun shine for killers.
phrases.notes: He means: give them hope and a way to be saved.

phrases.english: Some say He said to him:
You have made the sun shine for killers.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another אגדה about the ערי מקלט, now about משה setting them aside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערי מקלט 'make the sun shine' for accidental killers, giving them hope.

steps.title: משה grabbed a מצוה even when it would not work yet
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי reads 'one who loves silver is never satisfied' as describing משה, who set aside three cities even though they would not protect anyone until the other three were chosen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי סימאי taught: What does it mean, 'One who loves silver will never be satisfied with silver, and one who loves plenty will not have enough produce'? 'One who loves silver will never be satisfied with silver' is משה רבינו. He knew the three cities across the ירדן would not give refuge until three were chosen in ארץ כנען, and still he said: A מצוה that comes my way, I will do it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי סימאי explains a פסוק in קהלת as praise of משה's love for מצוות. Even a מצוה that would not take effect in his lifetime, he rushed to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha is that the three cities east of the ירדן do not protect anyone until the three in ארץ ישראל are also set aside, which happened only after משה died. משה knew this, but he still separated them, because he wanted every מצוה he could get. Like a person who loves money, he was never 'full' of מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: One who loves silver (here: loves מצוות)
The east side of the ירדן river
The land of Canaan, west of the ירדן
A מצוה that comes my way, I will do it

steps.whatToRemember: The three ערי מקלט across the ירדן did not work until the three in ארץ כנען were chosen, yet משה set them aside anyway out of love for מצוות.
steps.confusionAlert: משה's cities were not useless forever. They just did not start protecting anyone until the other three were chosen after he died.

phrases.english: רבי סימאי taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'One who loves silver will never be satisfied with silver,
phrases.notes: קהלת 5:9

phrases.english: and one who loves plenty will not have enough produce'?
'One who loves silver will never be satisfied with silver':
this is משה רבינו,
phrases.notes: Here the 'silver' he loves is מצוות; he can never get enough of them.

phrases.english: who knew that the three cities
across the ירדן do not give refuge

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְחֲרוּ שָׁלֹשׁ בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן,
phrases.english: until three are chosen in the land of Canaan,
and he said: A מצוה that has come my way, I will do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי סִימַאי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of משה setting aside the three cities from Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה set aside the eastern ערי מקלט, though they would not work yet, because he grabbed every מצוה that came his way.

steps.title: Only one who knows all of Torah should teach the public
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the פסוק in קהלת is read to mean that only someone who has all the Torah's 'produce' should teach a crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who loves a multitude, with no produce': who is fit to teach a crowd? Someone who has all the produce for himself, meaning he knows all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues reading the same פסוק from רבי סימאי's teaching, now looking at its second half. It explains it as a rule about who should teach Torah in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 read 'one who loves silver' as being about משה. Now 'multitude' (המון) is read as a crowd of students, and 'produce' (תבואה) as full knowledge of Torah. A teacher of the public needs to have all of it, not just part.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce or yield; here, a full store of Torah knowledge

phrases.english: "And who loves a multitude, with no produce":
phrases.notes: קהלת 5:9, the second half of the same פסוק used in step 24.

phrases.english: For whom is it fitting to teach a multitude?
One whom all the produce belongs to.
phrases.notes: He means someone who has all of the Torah's content in hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אֹהֵב בֶּהָמוֹן לֹא תְבוּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the same פסוק from קהלת, moving to its second half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only someone who knows all of Torah is fit to teach it to the public.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says the same thing from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'Who can express God's mighty acts, make all His praise heard' to mean that only one who can tell all of God's praise should speak of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רבי אלעזר said: what does it mean, 'Who can express the mighty acts of God, make all His praise heard'? Who is fit to speak of God's mighty acts? One who is able to tell all of His praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a matching teaching from רבי אלעזר that supports the idea of step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both teachings share one idea: speaking in public about holy things is fitting only for someone who has the whole picture. רבי אלעזר applies it to telling God's praise, which fits the rule about teaching Torah to a crowd.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "Who can express the mighty acts of God,
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:2

phrases.english: make all His praise heard"?
For whom is it fitting to express the mighty acts of God?
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'to teach' (round brackets); the corrected wording is 'to express' (square brackets), matching the פסוק.

phrases.english: One who is able to make all His praise heard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel teaching that supports step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that only one who knows everything should speak publicly.

steps.title: Whoever loves those who teach the public is rewarded
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן (or רבה בר מרי) read the פסוק as 'to him is produce': whoever loves one who teaches the public will be rewarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן, and some say רבה בר מרי, said: 'Who loves the multitude, to him is produce': whoever loves the one who teaches the multitude, he will have produce.
steps.whatsHappening: A second reading of the same words from קהלת. Here the פסוק is a promise of reward, not a warning about who may teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לא ('no') is read as לו ('to him'), which turns 'no produce' into 'he will have produce.' The one who gets the reward is not the teacher but whoever loves and supports the teacher of the public.

keyTerms.meaning: He will have produce, a reward

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, אָמַר:
phrases.english: And the Rabbis, and some say Rabba bar Mari, said:
"Who loves a multitude, to him is produce":
phrases.notes: Notice he reads the פסוק's לא ('no') as if it were לו ('to him').

phrases.english: whoever loves the one who teaches a multitude,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. The meaning is loving the person who teaches the crowd.

phrases.english: to him there will be produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same words that step 25 explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who loves a teacher of the public will be rewarded with 'produce'.

steps.title: The רבנן pointed to רבא son of רבה
steps.stepSummary: When the Sages heard this teaching, they looked at רבא son of רבה as a living example of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages set their eyes on רבא son of רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: A short story showing step 27 in real life: the Sages saw this blessing in רבא son of רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text does not say what he did. The point is that the Sages saw him as someone who received the 'produce' promised to those who love teachers of Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: They set their eyes on, they looked at

phrases.english: The Rabbis set their eyes
phrases.notes: They looked to him as the example of the teaching they had just heard.

phrases.english: on Rava, son of Rabba.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהַבוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן עֵינַיְיהוּ בְּרָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates step 27 with a real person.
steps.raayaObject: The promise of reward to those who love teachers of the public.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Sages' recognition of רבא son of רבה.

steps.title: A memory sign for the next two teachings
steps.stepSummary: A memory aid: רב אשי will speak about learning, and רבינא about teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: אשי 'to learn,' רבינא 'to teach.')
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a teaching. It is a memory sign that sets up the next two readings of the פסוק, so you can remember who said which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two more אמוראים will read the same words. רב אשי's reading is about learning with many people, and רבינא's (which comes later) is about teaching many people.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up לִלְמוֹד (to learn) with לְלַמֵּד (to teach). The whole memory sign depends on that one difference.

phrases.english: (Memory sign: Ashi "to learn,"
Ravina "to teach.")

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן: אָשֵׁי לִלְמוֹד, רָבִינָא לְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up two more readings of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory sign, not a ruling.

steps.title: רב אשי: whoever loves learning with others will succeed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the פסוק as: whoever loves to learn together with many people will have 'produce', meaning success.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: whoever loves to learn with many people, he will have produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third reading of the same words. He makes them about the value of learning in a group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'multitude' means study partners, not students. The reward goes to the learner himself who chooses to learn with others instead of alone.

keyTerms.meaning: To learn together with many people

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כׇּל הָאוֹהֵב לִלְמוֹד בֶּהָמוֹן
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Whoever loves to learn with a multitude,
to him there will be produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כׇּל הָאוֹהֵב לִלְמוֹד בֶּהָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first reading the memory sign pointed to: 'אשי – to learn'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning together with others brings success in learning.

steps.title: A sword on those who learn alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads 'a sword upon the בדים' as a sword on תלמידי חכמים who learn alone, בד בבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: what does 'a sword upon the בדים, and they will be foolish' mean? A sword on the necks of the enemies of תלמידי חכמים who sit and learn Torah alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב אשי with a teaching that warns harshly against learning alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בדים in ירמיהו is read like בד בבד, 'each one by himself.' If learning alone deserves a 'sword,' then learning with others (רב אשי's point) is the right way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The enemies of Torah scholars': a polite way to refer to the scholars themselves

steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemies of תלמידי חכמים' really means the scholars themselves. The גמרא just avoids saying a curse directly about them.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "A sword upon the baddim, and they will become foolish"?
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 50:36

phrases.aramaic: חֶרֶב עַל צַוְּארֵי שׂוֹנְאֵיהֶם שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים,
phrases.english: A sword on the necks of the enemies of Torah scholars,
who sit and occupy themselves with Torah each one alone.
phrases.notes: This is the play on words: בדים is read as בד בבד, 'alone'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רב אשי by showing that learning alone is harmful.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's teaching that learning with others is the right way.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 50:36 as read by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: Learning alone leads to foolishness and sin
steps.stepSummary: The word ונאלו is linked to 'אשר נואלנו' in במדבר, showing that those who learn alone grow foolish, and the same פסוק continues 'אשר חטאנו', showing they also sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that, they grow foolish: here it says 'ונאלו', and there it says 'that we were foolish'. And more than that, they sin, as it says 'and that we sinned'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא keeps going. He uses the last word of the פסוק to show two more harms of learning alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word in two places (ונאלו / נואלנו) shows that ונאלו means 'became foolish.' The פסוק in במדבר goes right on to 'we sinned,' so foolishness and sin are tied together.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also
It is written here… and it is written there: linking a word in two פסוקים

phrases.english: And not only that, but they become foolish:
It is written here: "and they will become foolish (veno'alu),"
and it is written there: "for we have been foolish (no'alnu)."
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:11

phrases.english: And not only that, but they sin,
as it is said: "and for we have sinned."
phrases.notes: These are the next words in that same פסוק in במדבר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּטַּפְּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reading, adding foolishness and sin.
steps.raayaObject: That learning alone leads to foolishness and then to sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word נואל in ירמיהו 50:36 and במדבר 12:11.

steps.title: Another source that נואלו means sinning
steps.stepSummary: Instead of במדבר, one can learn from ישעיהו's 'נואלו שרי צען' that נואלו means doing wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it from here: 'The princes of צען have acted foolishly.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different source for the idea that learning alone leads to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו, נואלו describes the princes of צען, who acted wrongly. That shows the word itself carries the meaning of sinning, without needing the next words in the פסוק in במדבר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another option
The princes of Zoan, a city in Egypt

steps.whatToRemember: So far the קהלת פסוק has been read three ways: only one who knows everything should teach the public; whoever loves teachers of the public is rewarded; and whoever loves learning with others succeeds. Learning alone leads to foolishness and even sin. רבינא adds a fourth reading in the next step.

phrases.english: And if you want, say it from here:
"The princes of Zoan have acted foolishly (no'alu)."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 19:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same point as the end of step 32.

steps.title: רבינא: whoever loves to teach many people will succeed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reads the פסוק as being about teaching many people, not learning with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא says: Anyone who loves to teach in front of many people will have 'produce', meaning he will grow and succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives his own reading of the same פסוק that רב אשי explained. This matches the memory aid from before: רבינא speaks about teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי read 'בהמון' as learning together with many people. רבינא reads it as teaching many people. In his reading, the teacher himself gains, because his own understanding grows.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach others (not just to learn)
In front of many people, to a crowd
Produce, crops; here it means success and growth in תורה

phrases.english: Ravina says:
Anyone who loves to teach before many people –
phrases.notes: He is reading the same פסוק רב אשי used: 'מי אוהב בהמון לא תבואה' (קהלת 5:9).

phrases.english: to him shall be produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: כׇּל הָאוֹהֵב לְלַמֵּד בֶּהָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבינא's reading of the פסוק, which differs from רב אשי's reading in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who loves to teach many people will grow and succeed in תורה.

steps.title: רבי learned the most from his students
steps.stepSummary: רבי's famous saying supports רבינא's idea that teaching makes the teacher grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי meant when he said: I learned much תורה from my teachers, more from my friends than from them, and more from my students than from all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects רבינא's idea to a well-known saying of רבי. רבי said he learned the most from his students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a teacher gains the most from his students, then teaching others really does bring 'produce'. Students ask questions and push the teacher to think harder. That is exactly how teaching makes the teacher grow.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same idea as...

steps.whatToRemember: Teaching others is not only giving. The teacher grows the most, as רבי said: 'from my students more than from all of them.'

phrases.english: And that is what Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: Much Torah have I learned from my teachers,
and from my friends more than from them,
and from my students more than from all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's reading with רבי's saying about learning from students.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's teaching that one who teaches many people grows from it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's saying that he learned more from his students than from his teachers or friends.

steps.title: Our feet stood firm in war because of Torah in Jerusalem's gates
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that the soldiers won their battles in the merit of the תורה learned in ירושלים's gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks what the פסוק 'Our feet were standing in your gates, ירושלים' means. He answers: What made our feet stand firm in war? The gates of ירושלים, where people were learning תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the theme of how great תורה learning is, רבי יהושע בן לוי explains a פסוק in תהלים. He reads it to mean that success in war came from the תורה learned in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken simply, the פסוק says 'our feet stood in your gates.' רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'בשעריך' as 'because of your gates.' The gates were where people learned תורה and judged, so the soldiers' strength came from that learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Your gates, the city gates where people learned and judged

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Our feet were standing in your gates, Jerusalem"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 122:2

phrases.english: What caused our feet to stand firm in war?
The gates of Jerusalem, where they were busy learning Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from learning with others to a new אגדה about the power of תורה learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The merit of the תורה learned in ירושלים's gates is what gave the soldiers strength in war.

steps.title: דוד rejoiced when people waited for שלמה to build the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: דוד tells הקדוש ברוך הוא that he heard people eager for his death so that שלמה would build the בית המקדש, and he was still happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains the פסוק 'I rejoiced when they said to me, let us go to the house of ה׳.' דוד said to הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, I heard people saying, 'When will this old man die, so that his son שלמה will come and build the בית המקדש and we can go up for the רגל?' And I was happy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a second teaching from the same chapter of תהלים. He tells what דוד said to הקדוש ברוך הוא, and the next step brings the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knew the בית המקדש would be built by דוד's son, not by דוד. So people's eagerness for the בית המקדש sounded like eagerness for דוד to die. Even so, דוד said he was happy, because they wanted to go to the house of ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: A Song of Ascents, the opening of several chapters of תהלים
The chosen house, meaning the בית המקדש
We will go up to ירושלים for the festival (עלייה לרגל)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"A Song of Ascents, of David:

phrases.aramaic: שָׂמַחְתִּי בְּאֹמְרִים לִי בֵּית ה׳ נֵלֵךְ״?
phrases.english: I rejoiced when they said to me, let us go to the house of God"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 122:1

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Master of the world, I heard people who were saying:
"When will this old man die,
phrases.notes: 'This old man' is דוד himself; the people were talking about him.

phrases.english: and Solomon his son will come
and build the Chosen House
and we will go up for the festival?"
And I rejoiced.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת לְדָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by the same רבי יהושע בן לוי, on the פסוק just before the one in step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד was happy that people longed for the בית המקדש, even though that meant longing for his own death.

steps.title: One day of דוד's תורה is better than a thousand קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers דוד that one day of his תורה learning is dearer than the thousand עולות שלמה will bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to him: 'For one day in your courtyards is better than a thousand.' One day that you spend learning תורה before Me is better to Me than the thousand עולות that your son שלמה will one day offer before Me on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers דוד's words from the previous step. He uses a פסוק to tell דוד that his own תורה learning matters more than the קרבנות of the future בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people were waiting for דוד to die so the קרבנות could begin. הקדוש ברוך הוא tells דוד not to rush: every extra day he lives and learns is worth more than שלמה's thousand עולות. This shows how highly תורה learning is valued, even above קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Your courtyards; read here as the time דוד spends learning before ה׳
Burnt offerings, which are burned completely on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: A single day of תורה learning is dearer to הקדוש ברוך הוא than a thousand קרבנות.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
"For one day in your courtyards is better than a thousand" –
phrases.notes: תהלים 84:11

phrases.english: better to Me is one day
in which you are learning Torah before Me,
than a thousand burnt offerings
phrases.notes: This points to the thousand עולות שלמה brought, as told in מלכים א 3:4.

phrases.english: that Solomon your son will one day offer before Me
upon the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: ״כִּי טוֹב יוֹם בַּחֲצֵרֶיךָ מֵאָלֶף״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives הקדוש ברוך הוא's reply to דוד's words in step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: דוד's implied question: should he be pained that people were waiting for his death so the בית המקדש could be built?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One day of דוד's תורה learning is dearer than the thousand עולות שלמה will offer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One day of דוד's תורה learning is dearer to הקדוש ברוך הוא than the thousand עולות שלמה will offer.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: roads aligned to the cities of refuge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words about roads leading to the ערי מקלט and starts to quote a ברייתא by רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And roads were lined up for them,' and so on. A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says:
steps.whatsHappening: After the side teachings about תורה, the גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה about roads to the ערי מקלט. This is a setup line: it opens a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, whose words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that clear roads were made between cities so that a person who killed by accident could reach a עיר מקלט. The גמרא now brings a ברייתא that will add details about these roads. The actual teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב continues after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on; shows that only the first words of the משנה are quoted
A teaching from the time of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not finish a thought. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's actual teaching comes right after it.

phrases.english: "And roads were lined up for them," etc.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְכֻוּוֹנוֹת לָהֶם דְּרָכִים וְכוּ׳. תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about תורה learning and returns to the משנה's discussion of the ערי מקלט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a ברייתא that will explain the משנה's rule about roads to the ערי מקלט.
